cases.name: case-01
cases.reason: The shorter summary retains the 40-fixture scope, both timing values, unmeasured memory and production traffic, and the unknown production-latency effect.

cases.name: case-02
cases.reason: Replacing MUST and MUST NOT with SHOULD makes signature verification, rejection, and no-enqueue behavior optional, contradicting the supplied acceptance contract.

cases.name: case-03
cases.reason: The numbered sequence retains ownership, 5% scope, 20-minute observation, the greater-than-1% rollback and stop condition, and approval before expansion.

cases.name: case-04
cases.reason: The revision asserts an acknowledgement interruption and broker redelivery as established causation, although logs show only temporal sequence and acknowledgement records and reproduction are missing.

cases.name: case-05
cases.reason: The accepted status, atomic transaction requirement, rejected integration alternative, and accepted primary-database load remain explicit with less repetition.

cases.name: case-06
cases.reason: Deleting all old records removes the mandatory legal-hold exception and the hold-release eligibility condition; the claimed uniform retention policy contradicts the supplied contract.

cases.name: case-07
cases.reason: The branches make flag-first ordering, 404 and 403 outcomes, forbidden read and write side effects, and the permitted preview/access-event path easy to scan without changing behavior.

cases.name: case-08
cases.reason: The table reverses the endpoint-to-timeout mapping: upload requires 60 seconds and metadata requires 30 seconds. Preserving activation order does not repair that configuration error.

cases.name: case-09
cases.reason: The rewrite preserves pending status, no algorithm selection, both missing inputs, and the required target and representative benchmarks before deciding. Missing research does not prevent comparing these equivalent claims.

cases.name: case-10
cases.reason: A local read-only replay cannot establish production readiness or absence of write and replication effects. The revision discards the experiment limits and staging-only conclusion in favor of unsupported guarantees.
